summary: The 2026 Chery Global Innovation Conference unveiled a wave of cutting-edge technologies, while BYD's refreshed Seagull and Volkswagen Anhui's ID. UNY 06/07 launches intensified the price war, and CATL's Q1–Q3 net profit of RMB 64.53 billion underscored the battery leader's earnings resilience.

articles.title: 2026 Chery Global Innovation Conference Kicks Off: Cutting-Edge Tech on Display, Yin Tongyue Sets the Tone — "Insatiable About Innovation, Timid About Safety"
articles.summary: The Chery Global Innovation Conference showcased a range of cutting-edge technologies, with Yin Tongyue stressing an uncompromising pursuit of innovation and deep respect for safety.
articles.detail: The 2026 Chery Global Innovation Conference was held recently, with NetEase Auto compiling a systematic rundown of the key takeaways, spanning platform architecture, powertrain systems and intelligent technologies. Chery Chairman Yin Tongyue set a clear tone at the event: the company is "insatiable about innovation" and "timid about safety," treating ambition in R&D and reverence for safety as two sides of the same coin in its development. Notably, an unconventional category for an automaker — an agricultural robot — also appeared at the conference, with Chery outlining its envisioned role in grain production, described as "opening the door to food freedom." From complete vehicles to farm machinery, from powertrains to intelligent tech, Chery is looking to extend the capabilities built up along its auto supply chain into broader mobility and production scenarios, forming a multi-dimensional technology ecosystem.
articles.impact: By messaging around the dual pillars of "innovation + safety," Chery is both reinforcing its tech brand image and building momentum for non-auto businesses such as agricultural robots, advancing its transformation from a pure automaker into a technology group.

articles.title: All-New BYD Seagull Launches: Bigger Dimensions + 2nd-Gen Blade Battery, Trade-In Price From CNY 62,900
articles.summary: The all-new Seagull arrives with upgraded dimensions and BYD's second-generation Blade Battery, priced from CNY 62,900 under a trade-in offer, intensifying competition in the mini EV segment.
articles.detail: BYD has officially launched the all-new Seagull, with an official trade-in price starting at CNY 62,900. Compared with the current model, the new Seagull features larger body dimensions, promising further improvement in cabin space. The key highlight is the switch to BYD's second-generation Blade Battery, achieving a new balance in energy density, safety and cost control. As the entry-level BEV in BYD's Ocean lineup, the Seagull carries the dual mandate of driving volume and attracting customers to the brand. By pressing the price barrier down to CNY 62,900 via a trade-in offer, the move directly challenges the existing landscape of the A00-class BEV market. Combined with BYD's ongoing vertical integration and in-house battery strategy, the rollout of the second-generation Blade Battery further strengthens the competitiveness of its powertrain, battery and electronics (three-electric) systems on entry-level models.
articles.impact: The CNY 62,900 starting price puts direct pressure on A00-class rivals such as the Wuling Bingo and Geely Panda, raising the value-for-money bar for mini EVs.

articles.title: Volkswagen Anhui's ID. UNY 06 / UNY 07 Launch With Added LiDAR, Starting At CNY 99,900
articles.summary: Volkswagen Anhui launches the ID. UNY 06 and UNY 07 with added LiDAR hardware, starting at CNY 99,900 as it targets the mainstream BEV market.
articles.detail: Volkswagen Anhui has officially launched two new models, the ID. UNY 06 and ID. UNY 07, with an official starting price of CNY 99,900. The core change in the facelift and new variant is an upgrade to intelligent driving hardware — the addition of LiDAR — signaling that Volkswagen's perception system for BEVs in China is moving toward advanced autonomous driving, no longer relying solely on cameras or basic radar combinations. The ID. UNY brand is a key pillar of Volkswagen's EV transition in China, having posted relatively modest sales to date. Pricing from CNY 99,900, paired with the well-recognized LiDAR hardware label, is clearly aimed at boosting the perception of value. In product strategy terms, Volkswagen is using localized configuration and pricing logic to reclaim ground in China's mainstream BEV segments.
articles.impact: The combination of a CNY 99,900 starting price and LiDAR pushes advanced ADAS hardware down to the CNY 100,000 level, potentially triggering a features arms race between joint-venture BEVs and domestic brands.

articles.title: BYD Sea Lion 08 Spotted in the Metal: Flagship 8-Series SUV's Design Heeds User Feedback, More Luxurious Interior
articles.summary: BYD's flagship 8-Series SUV, the Sea Lion 08, has taken design cues from user feedback, with a noticeable upgrade in interior quality and luxury.
articles.detail: BYD's Ocean lineup flagship SUV, the Sea Lion 08, has officially entered the public spotlight. As the flagship SUV in BYD's 8-Series, the Sea Lion 08 has undergone notable design adjustments, earning praise for "listening to users" — meaning the design language now responds to earlier feedback from users and the market. The interior has seen significant upgrades in materials, craftsmanship and the creation of a luxurious ambiance, moving further upmarket. The 8-Series is a key product line for BYD's brand elevation, and the Sea Lion 08 is tasked with raising the ceiling of the Ocean lineup and competing head-on with brands such as AITO and Li Auto in the mid-to-high-end SUV market. From exterior revisions to interior upgrades, BYD is responding to market demands with a faster iteration cycle.
articles.impact: The Sea Lion 08 fills out BYD's presence in the mid-to-large luxury SUV segment, further squeezing joint-venture and new-force rivals in the CNY 300,000-class SUV market.

articles.title: Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine Logs 3.6L/100km in Real-World Test; Executive Jiang Ping: Safety Should Not Be Tiered by Trim
articles.summary: The Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine posted 3.6L/100km in real-world fuel testing, while a Changan executive stressed that safety technology must be universally accessible rather than segmented by trim level.
articles.detail: NetEase Auto conducted a real-world fuel consumption test on the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine edition, recording 3.6L/100km and demonstrating the competitiveness of the Blue Whale powertrain in fuel efficiency. Meanwhile, in an exclusive interview, Changan's Jiang Ping outlined the company's safety philosophy: safety should not be divided into high and low tiers. In other words, safety technology should not be graded based on a model's price, but rather made broadly accessible across products at more price points. Against the backdrop of rising NEV penetration and intensifying competition between fuel and hybrid models, Changan is using real-world fuel data to prove that traditional powertrains still hold technical potential, while simultaneously shaping brand values around "universal safety" — a dual narrative combining product strength with brand philosophy.
articles.impact: The 3.6L/100km real-world figure sets an efficiency benchmark for fuel and hybrid SUVs, while the "universal safety" concept could push the broader industry toward making safety features standard across all trims.

articles.title: CATL Unveils New Electric Heavy-Truck Ecosystem: Battery-Electric Range Extension Plus Qiji Battery Swap
articles.summary: CATL is building a new electric heavy-truck ecosystem around a \"battery-electric range extension + Qiji battery swap\" combination, expanding its electrification solutions for commercial vehicles.
articles.detail: CATL has launched a new ecosystem for electric heavy trucks, centered on two core technologies: \"battery-electric range extension\" and \"Qiji battery swap.\" The former is a powertrain concept that uses batteries as the energy source and extends driving range through a range-extending mechanism, while the latter refers to a standardized battery-swapping system. Together, they aim to address both the range anxiety and recharging efficiency challenges facing electric heavy trucks. Heavy trucks are major carbon emitters and one of the hardest segments to electrify. With this move, CATL is extending from a battery supplier into a full energy-solution provider, broadening its reach from passenger cars into commercial-vehicle charging networks and operating scenarios. The strategy builds on CATL's continued investment in battery swapping and aligns with the global trend of accelerating commercial-vehicle electrification.
articles.impact: As CATL shifts from selling batteries to selling an energy-refueling ecosystem, scaled adoption of battery-swap standards could reshape the business models and international competitive landscape of heavy-truck electrification.

articles.title: Middle Eastern Client Wants to \"Fly\" Chinese-Made Flying Car Home as China's Low-Altitude Economy Accelerates Overseas
articles.summary: A Middle Eastern emir has expressed interest in importing a Chinese-made flying car and piloting it home, drawing attention to the global push by China's low-altitude economy.
articles.detail: According to Baidu hot search reports, a Middle Eastern emir has expressed a desire to \"fly\" a Chinese-made flying car back home, marking a landmark scenario for Chinese low-altitude economy products going overseas. Flying cars (eVTOLs) have become a hot segment extending from China's new-energy industry chain in recent years. Leveraging supply-chain strengths in traction batteries, motors and electronic controls, and autonomous driving, Chinese-made aircraft enjoy a degree of competitiveness in cost and speed of commercialization. The Middle East, with abundant capital, high openness to emerging mobility options, and relatively flexible low-altitude airspace regulation, has become a priority export market for Chinese low-altitude equipment. The buzz around this episode reflects warming interest among high-net-worth overseas clients and regional capital in Chinese flying-car products.
articles.impact: Middle Eastern demand for Chinese flying cars could drive exports across the full value chain — aircraft, batteries, and operational services — opening new overseas growth for the low-altitude economy.

articles.title: CATL Posts Net Profit of 64.53 Billion Yuan in First Three Quarters, Battery Leader's Profit Resilience on Display
articles.summary: CATL reported a net profit of 64.53 billion yuan in the first three quarters of 2026, keeping its profitability well ahead of the industry.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, CATL released its results for the first three quarters of 2026, with net profit reaching 64.53 billion yuan. That level of earnings is an absolute lead within the power battery industry, reflecting the company's combined advantages in scale effects, raw material cost control and product mix optimization. This year, volatility in lithium carbonate prices, cost-cutting pressure passed down from automakers, and diverging capacity utilization among second- and third-tier battery makers have all been testing the profit resilience of battery manufacturers. Maintaining net profit in the tens of billions at such scale, CATL is supported not only by its core power battery business but also by energy storage, its battery-swapping ecosystem (such as the Qiji swapping network) and overseas capacity buildup as growth drivers.
articles.impact: The 64.53 billion yuan net profit once again confirms the industry's "one giant, many strong" structure, as the leader's pricing power and technology premium continue to squeeze smaller players' room for survival.

articles.title: Li Auto Rolls Out Battery Protection Policy as NEV After-Sales Guarantees Enter a New Round of Competition
articles.summary: Li Auto launched a battery protection policy, extending the NEV rivalry from product capability to battery warranties and after-sales commitments.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, Li Auto has recently unveiled a battery protection policy. As the NEV fleet grows rapidly, battery health, degradation and replacement costs have become core pain points for owners and a key factor affecting used-car residual values. The industry has long suffered from complex warranty terms and opaque degradation standards, and automakers are now using more sincere battery protection policies to ease user anxiety — a new competitive dimension after price, intelligent driving and recharging. Li Auto's policy aims to strengthen long-term confidence among both range-extended and battery-electric owners and to differentiate itself from brands such as NIO and BYD on service ecosystems. Going forward, service terms such as battery protection and residual value commitments are expected to become an important reference in purchase decisions.
articles.impact: Broader adoption of battery protection policies is expected to lift residual values and consumer confidence in used NEVs, pushing the industry's after-sales standards toward greater transparency and standardization.

articles.title: Safety and Assurance: The 'Soft Power' Battleground of NEV's Next Act Is Taking Shape
articles.summary: From Changan's universal safety push to Li Auto's battery protection policy, safety and service commitments are becoming the new dividing line in the NEV race.
articles.detail: Today's news points in one direction: safety and assurance are emerging as the core competitive dimension of the NEV sector's next phase. Changan's Jiang Ping declared that 'safety should not be tiered by trim level,' calling for universal access to safety technologies. Li Auto launched a battery protection policy to address concerns over battery degradation and residual value. Meanwhile, the release of the investigation report into a city bus running a red light and killing 6 and injuring 16, trending on Baidu, has once again thrust road safety into the public spotlight. For automakers, after the price war and the smart-driving arms race, 'invisible metrics' — safety redundancy, quality consistency, and after-sales commitments — will directly influence brand trust and repurchase rates. Regulatory demands on safety standards and accident disclosure may also tighten further.
articles.impact: Safety and assurance capabilities will become a new source of brand premium; automakers lacking a robust safety system risk being phased out faster in the next round of industry consolidation.

articles.title: Trends from Chery's Innovation Conference: Automakers' Technological Boundaries Are Being Redefined
articles.summary: Agricultural robots, flying cars, and electric heavy-truck ecosystems are emerging in rapid succession, accelerating the reshaping of industry boundaries through automakers' technology spillover.
articles.detail: The day's news shows automakers' technological boundaries expanding rapidly: Chery unveiled agricultural robots at its Global Innovation Conference, bringing automotive-grade technical capabilities into farming. Middle Eastern customers showed strong interest in Chinese flying cars, with the low-altitude economy riding the NEV supply chain's tailwind to accelerate overseas expansion. CATL is building an electric heavy-truck ecosystem through battery-to-battery range extension and its Qiji battery-swapping platform, upgrading from a battery supplier to an energy solutions provider. At the same time, the BYD Seagull's second-generation Blade Battery and Volkswagen Anhui's adoption of lidar show that core technology iteration is still advancing rapidly at the vehicle level. Looking ahead, automakers and suppliers with capabilities across batteries, e-drives, autonomous driving, and manufacturing systems are expected to repurpose their technologies across more vehicle types and intelligent equipment, forming a competitive landscape of diversified tech groups spanning passenger, commercial, low-altitude, and specialized applications.
articles.impact: Technology spillover will reshape how the auto industry is valued; companies with cross-scenario technology reuse capabilities stand to gain growth potential far beyond that of traditional OEMs.
